attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses the financial assertion himself.

semantics.note: The normalization faithfully extracts the factual financial assertion from the surrounding acquisition recommendation.

contract.note: The reporting window and profitability measure are evaluator-supplied but reasonable operationalizations of the ordinary reading. Allowing occasional profitable periods preserves 'mostly'; examining the industry separately preserves its broader scope.

evidence.note: Anthropic's timely company disclosure reports net losses throughout the target reporting periods. Large noncash financing revaluations explain much of their size. One profitable operating quarter does not establish sustained company-wide profitability.

Reporting based on audited statements supports OpenAI's 2025 losses, including after excluding the restructuring charge. It does not cover first-half 2026. Publication preceded the cutoff despite later retrieval.

Positive adjusted earnings qualify the financial picture but use a different measure. The reported first-half operating loss and excluded compensation and financing costs prevent treating adjusted profit as decisive contradiction.
The research documents limited financial disclosure across AI labs. That measurement gap does not establish whether sustained profitability had been demonstrated across the relevant industry.

reviews.rationale: Reported losses support the company-level assertion, with substantial noncash charges requiring qualification. The unspecified accounting basis does not disqualify reported net results under this ordinary-reading contract. However, OpenAI's first-half 2026 results are incomplete, and the packet cannot settle the separate industry-wide assertion. Adjusted profits and one profitable quarter do not establish contradiction.
